symptoms: Small, water-soaked, dark spots on foliage

Fruit spots enlarging, turning brown, raised, scab-like, and heavily textured
causes: Spread via sprinkler irrigation or rain splash

medium: Stop watering the plants from above (use drip irrigation if possible)

monitoringAdvice: Inspect foliage for small, water-soaked, dark spots lacking concentric rings
Check developing fruits for raised, brown, scab-like spots
farmerFriendlyExplanation: A bacterial infection spread by water splashing dirt onto the leaves. It creates small, raised, black, scabby spots on both the leaves and the green tomatoes, completely ruining the fruit for sale. The farmer must stop watering from above, pull out infected plants, and spray a mixture of copper and streptomycin. Locally called జీవాణు ధబ్బా (Jiwanu dhabba) in Hindi and బాక్టీరియా మచ్చ (Bacteria macha) in Telugu.

farmerFriendlyExplanation: Blight is a serious fungal disease that damages tomato leaves, stems, and fruits. It spreads rapidly during cool and wet weather. Early signs include brown spots and yellowing leaves. Severe infections may cause greasy black patches, white fungal growth under leaves, and fruit rot. Immediate removal of infected leaves and timely fungicide spraying are critical to prevent major crop loss.

Olive-green to grayish velvety mold on the corresponding lower (abaxial) leaf surfaces
Lesions rapidly coalescing, causing the foliage to undergo severe chlorosis, necrosis, and premature defoliation
Significantly reduced plant photosynthetic capacity
earlySymptoms: Pale green to yellowish spots appearing on the upper surfaces of the older, lower leaves
advancedSymptoms: Olive-green to grayish velvety mold developing on the corresponding lower (abaxial) leaf surfaces
Severe chlorosis, necrosis, and premature defoliation
causes: Passalora fulva (syn. Fulvia fulva) fungal pathogen
Pathogen overwintering in infected crop debris

farmerFriendlyExplanation: Tomato leaf mold is a fungus that thrives in very humid, sticky weather, especially inside greenhouses. It creates yellow spots on top of the leaves and an olive-green fuzzy mold underneath. Prune the bottom leaves to let the wind blow through, stop watering from above, and spray a recommended fungicide directly onto the undersides of the leaves. In local languages, it is called टमाटर का लीफ मोल्ड (Tamatar ka leaf mold) in Hindi and టమాటా ఆకు బూజు (Tamata aaku booju) in Telugu.

farmerFriendlyExplanation: Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot is a fungus that causes many tiny, round grey spots with dark borders on the lowest tomato leaves. It spreads upward when rain or irrigation splashes dirt onto the plant. It will cause all the leaves to turn yellow and fall off. The immediate action is to physically remove the diseased bottom leaves, mulch the soil to prevent mud splashing, and spray a protectant fungicide. It is known as सेप्टोरिया पत्ती धब्बा (Septoria patti dhabba) in Hindi and సెప్టోరియా ఆకు మచ్చ (Septoria aaku macha) in Telugu.
